Player thrust control input POTIN is from the wiper ofa 5 K-ohm potentiometer connected between +5 VDC and ground, The POTIN signal varies from +2 to +35 VDC, depending on the position ofthe thust control. Ths voltage is compared with the output of digital-to-analog (DIA) converter N10 atthe pin 9 and 10 inputs of comparator RUT. Ifthe POTIN voltage R11, pin 10); greater than the DIA converter output (R1, pin 9), pin 8 of R11 goes high. Ifthe POTIN voltage is lower than the D/A converter output voltage, pin 8 of RTT goes low. ‘The DIA converter output voltage is controlled by the digital input (INDO thru IND7) from <downlup counters P3 and P10. The counters count up when pin 8 of R11 is low and count down ‘when pin & of Rit is high. This feedback loop results ina self calibrating “pot voltage seek” ci. ‘uit The counters continuously count up or down as they “seek the count which will cause the D/A output voltage to be equal tothe POTIN voltage. The MPU can then read the count output of counters P9 and PIO (via wstate buffer NB and the POTIN address), determine the relative positon ofthe thrust contro, and output data to the ‘vector generator circuit forthe thust picture and to the audio circuit for the thrust sound.
